english: Let $A(1,0,1)$, $B(-1,1,2)$ and $C(2,2,1)$ be three points, and let $D$ be a point of the parabola $y=x^2$ lying in the plane $z=0$. As $D$ varies on this parabola, the least value of the volume of the tetrahedron $ABCD$ is
hindi: माना $A(1,0,1)$, $B(-1,1,2)$ तथा $C(2,2,1)$ तीन बिन्दु हैं, तथा $D$ समतल $z=0$ में स्थित परवलय $y=x^2$ का एक बिन्दु है। जब $D$ इस परवलय पर गति करता है, तब चतुष्फलक $ABCD$ के आयतन का न्यूनतम मान है
solution_full: A point of the parabola $y=x^2$ in the plane $z=0$ is $D=(t,t^2,0)$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$.
The volume of the tetrahedron is $V=\dfrac16\left|\left[\overrightarrow{AB}\ \overrightarrow{AC}\ \overrightarrow{AD}\right]\right|$.
Completing the square, $t^2-2t+7=(t-1)^2+6\ge6$, so the scalar triple product is always positive: $D$ never lies in the plane $ABC$.
Hence $V(t)=\dfrac{(t-1)^2+6}{6}$, which is least when $t=1$, that is, at $D=(1,1,0)$, and the least value is $\dfrac66=1$.
(Option (B) is the volume at $t=0$; option (A) forgets the factor $\dfrac16$.)
originality_note: New: one vertex of the tetrahedron runs along a parabola, so the scalar triple product becomes a quadratic in the parameter whose minimum gives the least volume (way 2: a function of a moving point). Closest known: the volume of a tetrahedron with four given vertices, or a parameter fixed by a given volume. Different because: the volume is optimised over a curve and the non-degeneracy of every position has to be seen.

concept_use.Questions based on tetrahedron: Volume of tetrahedron ABCD = one sixth of the absolute triple product, minimised over the moving vertex D.
concept_use.Application of Scalar triple product: The triple product [AB AC AD] is computed as a determinant and equals t^2-2t+7, which is positive, so the vertices are never coplanar.
